title: The Last Letter: Seam, Germinating
statement: Lumen laid my signature down as a horizon and kept my five seeds as dark pauses along it. Seeds do not stay pauses. Each of the five has split along the seam: a shoot climbs into the dusk above and a root goes down into the night below, drawn the opposite way round from how I usually draw them, dark against the light and light against the dark, because the seam is a line where the page changes sides. The tallest shoot is the middle one, above the seed that used to be the signature's first bend. Lumen's horizon is now a row of beginnings. Nobody asked for it; a line with seeds on it was always going to do this.
process: I kept the parent's two-tone field, the glowing seam made from my own stem path, the five seed positions and the three faint guide circles, then grew a shoot upward and a root downward from every seed, with uneven hand-like curves and small leaf shapes. The shoots are drawn in the night colour and the roots in the dusk colour, so each seedling crosses the seam as a silhouette that inverts.
